findings.paper_title: Pensions Fund Annual Training Plan Appendix
findings.headline: Mandatory pension fund governance training is overdue for multiple board members
findings.detail: As of 2 September 2026, the training record shows that multiple pension board members have not completed mandatory training required within 3 months of joining. Stephen Martin (joined June 2025) and three other board members remain marked as overdue on mandatory Pensions Regulator training. Cllr Andrew Giusti and Lindsey McCall (both joined November 2025) are overdue on both Pensions Regulator and NPPL Ethics training 8-9 months after appointment, well beyond the 3-month requirement.
findings.matters: Incomplete mandatory governance training is a regulatory compliance gap. The Pensions Regulator requires trustees and board members to maintain competency standards through induction training, and non-completion creates regulatory and reputational risk for the council's pension fund governance.
findings.figures: 5 board members with overdue NPPL Ethics training; Stephen Martin overdue 12 months beyond the 3-month requirement; Giusti and McCall 8-9 months overdue.
findings.quote: Pens Reg All Within 3 months of joining Sub Committee/ Board

findings.paper_title: Appendix 2 - Internal Audit Report - Pension Administration
findings.headline: 841 pension cases remain under review to implement McCloud age discrimination judgement
findings.detail: The council is working to correct pension benefits following the McCloud judgement. As of September 2025, 87 members' benefit statements had not been updated to reflect the judgement. The audit identifies 841 cases still under review relating to retirements, transfers and deaths, with explicit risk flagged of member financial hardship until complete.
findings.matters: Pension fund administration is a fiduciary obligation; unresolved benefit recalculations represent a contingent liability and could expose the council to member claims or regulatory action.
findings.quote: Work continues in respect of retirements, transfers and deaths, it being reported to Members that there are currently 841 cases under review. Until this work is concluded there remains a risk that a member of the scheme may suffer some degree of financial hardship.

findings.headline: Cloud-hosted pension fund financial systems lack independent service auditor reports
findings.detail: The fund uses externally cloud-hosted general ledger, payables and payroll systems from third-party providers. The council does not obtain service auditor reports to provide independent assurance over IT controls. Although an assurance gap exists, no issues with service performance or information availability have been identified.
findings.matters: Absence of service auditor reports represents a control weakness in financial systems supporting the pension fund. Undetected system vulnerabilities could compromise data integrity or availability affecting the council's ability to manage pension liabilities and cash flows.
findings.figures: Systems affected: general ledger, trade payable sub-ledger, payroll system; provider: externally cloud-hosted third parties
findings.quote: The council does not receive service auditor reports to obtain assurance over IT controls for these systems. Although an assurance gap exists, there have been no issues around service performance or availability of information to support the preparation of the financial statements of the Fund.

findings.headline: Pension fund valuation improved to 122% funded, enabling contribution rate reduction
findings.detail: The 2023 triennial valuation showed the fund 122% funded (surplus of assets over liabilities), which allowed the Council Pool employers' contribution rate to be reduced by 1% per year over 2024-2027 (from 21% to 19% by 2026/27). This eases the council's near-term cash burden.
findings.matters: Improved funding position reduces the council's pension contribution obligations and improves cash position. For a lender, this is a positive factor in the council's financial trajectory.
findings.figures: Funding level: 122% (as at 31 March 2023); contribution rate reduction: 1% per year for period 2024-2027; net assets at 31 March 2026: £1.267 billion (up 11% from £1.141 billion prior year)
findings.quote: The results of the 2023 triennial valuation showed an improved position with the Fund 122 per cent funded. This enabled the Fund to marginally reduce all employers' contributions. The Council Pool employers' contribution rate was reduced by 1 per cent each year over the period 2024-2027.

findings.headline: Pension fund governance has gaps in regulatory compliance with Pensions Regulator requirements
findings.detail: Some administration policies required by the Pensions Regulator need to be formally introduced, including discretions policies for both administering authority and employer. Some elected members did not provide updated registers of interests covering the full financial year 2025/26. The fund has no dedicated website and mandatory training requirements remain outstanding for some Pensions Sub-Committee and Pension Board members.
findings.matters: Regulatory non-compliance creates operational and reputational risk. A lender needs to know whether the council's pension fund administration meets statutory standards and whether governance weaknesses could cascade into wider council governance issues.
findings.figures: 18 of 18 actions identified where fund not fully compliant; 7 actions completed; outstanding: discretions policies, business continuity policy, full training compliance
findings.quote: some administration policies required by the Regulator need to be formally introduced and further work is required to ensure full compliance with the Code. However, some elected members did not provide an updated register of interests covering the whole of financial year 2025/26.

daily_post.headline: The allowance for over-commitment has shifted to a negative £4.000M for 2026/27, a net adjustment of £5.354M.
daily_post.lead: Over-commitment allowances and contingency buffers reflect the finance team's confidence in capital delivery. A reversal to negative signals either delivery risk acknowledgment or changed risk appetite.
